title: No one has sins actually remitted before true faith and serious repentance
source_text: XVII. Et hinc quoque manifestum est nemini peccata actu remissa esse priusquam per veram fidem, & seriam poenitentiam ad Deum conversus fuerit. Cujus contrarium tamen Theologi nonnulli videntur asserere. Sed in eo vel male sentiunt, vel non bene loquuntur. Nam quicunque peccato servit, & in Christum non credit, ira Dei manet super eum, sententia Dei damnatus est, a Deo dicitur, manet in morte, necdum transiit a morte ad vitam. Peccato autem servit, & in Christum non credit, qui nondum est ad Deum per fidem & poenitentiam conversus. Quis autem capere valeat haec duo simul consistere posse, ut actu alicui peccata remissa sint, & tamen ille maneat in morte, & ira Dei maneat super eum?
pass_a_gloss: And hence it is also manifest that to no one are sins actually remitted before he has been converted to God through true faith and serious repentance. Yet some theologians seem to assert the contrary. But in that they either think badly or speak badly. For whoever serves sin and does not believe in Christ—the wrath of God remains upon him; he is condemned by God’s sentence; he is said by God to remain in death and has not yet passed from death to life. But he serves sin and does not believe in Christ who has not yet been converted to God through faith and repentance. But who can grasp that these two can stand together at once: that sins are actually remitted to someone, and yet he remains in death, and the wrath of God remains upon him?
pass_b_english: Actual remission never precedes true faith and serious repentance.
Serving sin / unbelief = wrath remaining and death—cannot coexist with actual pardon.

choices.why: Opposed to remaining in death under wrath.
